explanations.explanation: Obey, friend. God says, "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant…" (Jeremiah 11:3). Not just hear them, not just nod at them. Obey is the word that carries the whole message.

Copying sounds like a fine, tidy job, and I've copied plenty of cookie shapes. But God doesn't say "copy" here. He says, "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant…" (Jeremiah 11:3). Doing what He says is the point.

Reciting is a good guess, since saying words out loud feels so official. I once recited a whole recipe and still burned the batch, so I know how that goes. God's word here is obey: "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant…" (Jeremiah 11:3).

explanations.answer: They would be His people and He their God
explanations.explanation: That's it. God told them, "Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God." (Jeremiah 11:4). No prize list, just Him and His people together. That's about the best deal anybody ever got offered.

explanations.answer: They would never lose a single battle again
explanations.explanation: Sounds mighty, I'll give you that. But God never says a word about battles in this verse. He says, "Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God." (Jeremiah 11:4).

explanations.answer: They would rule over every nation on earth
explanations.explanation: Ruling every nation would be a big promise, friend, and it's not the one on the table. God said, "Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God." (Jeremiah 11:4). The promise is about belonging to Him.

True. God says He was establishing "…the oath I swore to your forefathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey…" (Jeremiah 11:5). He made a promise and put an oath on it. And the verse adds that the land is theirs "…as it is to this day."

Careful, friend, this one is true. God says it was "…in order to establish the oath I swore to your forefathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is to this day." (Jeremiah 11:5). He swore it, and He gave the land.
Once? Oh no, no, no. God says, "…I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’" (Jeremiah 11:7). That's a whole lot of warnings, and it was never a one-time thing.

False is right. God says, "…I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’" (Jeremiah 11:7). Again and again is a lot more than once, and it covers the time from Egypt until that day.

explanations.answer: The stubbornness of his evil heart
explanations.explanation: Yes. The verse says, "…each one followed the stubbornness of his evil heart." (Jeremiah 11:8). They wouldn't obey or incline their ears, and that's what they followed instead. That's a hard one to read, friend.

explanations.answer: The advice of the foreign kings
explanations.explanation: Reasonable guess, but the verse never mentions foreign kings. It says, "…each one followed the stubbornness of his evil heart." (Jeremiah 11:8). The text points at the heart of each person.

explanations.answer: The teaching of the false prophets
explanations.explanation: False prophets would make a good villain, but they aren't named in this verse. God says, "…each one followed the stubbornness of his evil heart." (Jeremiah 11:8). Each person followed their own heart instead of Him.

True. God says, "So I brought on them all the curses of this covenant I had commanded them to follow but they did not keep." (Jeremiah 11:8). That's a heavy line. The verse says they did not keep the covenant, and the curses came.

This one is true, friend, and it's a heavy one. God says, "So I brought on them all the curses of this covenant I had commanded them to follow but they did not keep." (Jeremiah 11:8). They didn't keep it, and the curses came.
True. God says, "They have returned to the sins of their forefathers who refused to obey My words." (Jeremiah 11:10). They went right back to what the forefathers did. That's a tough thing to hear.
It's actually true, friend. God says, "They have returned to the sins of their forefathers who refused to obey My words." (Jeremiah 11:10). They went back to the very sins their forefathers had.

explanations.answer: The house of Israel and the house of Judah
explanations.explanation: Right. God says, "The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers." (Jeremiah 11:10). Both houses are named. Nobody gets left out of that sentence.
Judah is in there, but not alone. God says, "The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers." (Jeremiah 11:10). Both houses are named, friend.

Israel is named, but it has company. God says, "The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers." (Jeremiah 11:10). Judah is right there in the same sentence.

explanations.answer: To the gods they burn incense to
explanations.explanation: Yes. God says they "…will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense…" (Jeremiah 11:12). They head for the gods they've been serving. And the verse says right away that those gods will not save them.

explanations.answer: To the king of Egypt for help
explanations.explanation: Egypt makes a good guess, since it's in this passage's history. But this verse sends them somewhere else. They "…will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense…" (Jeremiah 11:12).

explanations.answer: To the priests at the temple
explanations.explanation: Not the priests, friend. The verse says they "…will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense…" (Jeremiah 11:12). The cry goes to the gods they've been serving.

Not quite, friend. The verse says, "…these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:12). Judah will go and cry out to the gods they have been burning incense to. Those gods certainly will not save them.

False is right. God says, "…these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:12). The very gods they've been burning incense to will not save them. The verse says so plainly.

Not this time, friend. God tells Jeremiah, "…do not pray for these people. Do not raise up a cry or a prayer on their behalf…" (Jeremiah 11:14). He says He will not be listening when they call out to Him in their time of disaster.

Right, it's false. God says, "…do not pray for these people. Do not raise up a cry or a prayer on their behalf, for I will not be listening when they call out to Me in their time of disaster." (Jeremiah 11:14). That's a hard word for Jeremiah to carry.
True. God says, "When you are wicked, then you rejoice." (Jeremiah 11:15). I think it's a sad line. It's what God says about them in that verse.
It's true, friend, and a sad one. God says, "When you are wicked, then you rejoice." (Jeremiah 11:15). That's His own description of them.

That's the one. God says, "…with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). The tree was once called beautiful, and that makes the fire a hard picture to look at.

Chopping is how I'd picture it too, but that's not what the verse says. It says, "…with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). Fire is the picture.

Roots feel like a natural guess, since the tree was planted. But the verse goes another way: "…with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed." (Jeremiah 11:16). Fire is what the verse says will happen to the tree.

Planted. The verse says, "The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you…" (Jeremiah 11:17). Planted is the exact word the verse uses. He's the one who put them in the ground, so the olive tree picture fits together.

Found sounds sweet, like stumbling onto a good thing. But the verse says, "The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you…" (Jeremiah 11:17). Planted is the word, and it fits the tree.
Bought is a fair guess, friend. I got bought for a quarter myself! But Jeremiah 11:17 says, "The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you…" He planted them, like a tree.
